newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pound hits 52-month high of 200 yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Pound hits 52-month high of 200 yen in Tokyo.

text.p: *Sterling surged to 52-month high of 200 yen in cross-trading, its highest since October 1992, on massive wave of buying by Japanese securities firms in connection with dual-currency bonds, although it later fell back on profit-taking. Dollar gains on yen also helped.

*Strong interest from individual investors in higher-yielding investments behind bids, with gradual shift likely from Australian-dollar assets to sterling-denominated assets, one British bank dealer said.

*Although some in market talking of sterling rising as high as 200.50 yen, this unlikely, with around 200.10 yen likely to become high for now due to technical factors and sense that pound may have been overbought, he added.
*Buying of pounds for marks by U.S. securities firms also gave sterling a lift, one Japanese trust bank dealer said.

*Dollar powered above 123 yen, a fresh four-year high, then rose to around 123.18 yen by late Tokyo, on some short-covering after knock-out options placed around 123 yen disappeared, although profit-taking pushed it back under 123 yen again.
*Dollar hit 123 yen, new four-year high in afternoon Tokyo, riding wave of buying, largely from interbank operators, with bids from institutional investors as well.
*Some stop-loss bids triggered near 122.80-85 yen also helped greenback gain, along with heavy buying of pounds and marks for yen in cross-trading.
*Although fairly large offers around 123 yen flat knocked greenback slightly lower, dealers said room still remains for more gains.
